Common.IdempotencyKeyHeader.name: Idempotency-Key
Common.IdempotencyKeyHeader.description:
Client-chosen retry key, unique per intended create. A repeat with the same
key and body answers the resource the first one created, in its current
version, or creates it again once it was deleted; the same key with a
different body is refused with 409 while that resource exists. Deleting the
resource releases its key; keys expire after 24 hours.

Common.IfMatchHeader.name: If-Match
Common.IfMatchHeader.description:
The `etag` of the version being changed. A request without it is refused
with 428 Precondition Required; a request whose tag is no longer current is
refused with 412 Precondition Failed.

anything.

Mcp.Tools.TriageInput.description: Start of an investigation and the list of failures: the window's failures with their recorded status, new ones first and then by count, each labeled by how it changed against a baseline (new, worsening, ongoing, recovering, or regressed after being resolved), plus the operations whose error rate, p95 latency or throughput regressed, the releases first seen in the window and the silent services. The default window is the last 60 minutes, so pass a `lookback_minutes` or `start_time` that covers the incident; the baseline defaults to the window of equal length just before, and `status` defaults to `open`, the failures that need attention. A service is silent when its last span over the baseline and the window is older than the window's end minus 15 minutes or five of its usual intervals between spans, whichever is longer. The nami MCP server's own telemetry, service `nami.mcp`, is left out unless `service_name` names it. Explain a failure with get_failure_context and record a decision on it with update_failure_status.

Mcp.Tools.UpdateFailureStatusInput.description: Records a triage decision on one failure: status `open`, `resolved` or `ignored`, an optional assignee and, for `ignored`, an optional `ignore_until`. Each call replaces all three and needs the failure's current `etag`; the stored failure returns with its new etag. Triage then reports a resolved failure that recurs as `regressed` and leaves an ignored one out until its `ignore_until`, if any, passes. Needs the nami:write scope; telemetry is not changed.

Mcp.Tools.VerifyFixInput.description: Checks whether a fix held: counts the failure's occurrences and its operation's requests before and after the change and answers `passed`, `failed` (it recurred), `pending` (fewer than `min_requests` requests or `min_minutes` minutes since the change) or `inconclusive`. Give exactly one of `failure_id` or `matchers` (the matched spans are the requests and their errors the failures), and a `since` time or a `release` of the failure's service whose first span marks the change; `change` names the anchor used. The before window runs from the failure's first retained occurrence (with `matchers`: from the change minus the lookback) to the change, the after window from the change to now. Repeat the check later with the returned `verify_id`.
